item.title: The Daily Shot Brief – October 2, 2026
item.description: This is the Daily Shot Brief, an abridged version of The Daily Shot.
item.dc:creator: TDS Infinity
item.content:encoded:
This is the Daily Shot Brief, an abridged version of The Daily Shot. If you would like to subscribe to the full-length Daily Shot (see example), please register here.

United States

Construction spending on data centers is going parabolic.

Euro Area

France unveiled a €54 billion fiscal consolidation plan—including €43 billion in new measures and €11 billion from previously enacted measures—to cut its deficit to 5% of GDP in 2027 from 5.4% this year.

The public debt burden is expected to surpass 120% of GDP next year.

Emerging Markets

Chile’s economic activity fell for a second month, pulled lower by a sharp decline in mining activity due to weather and maintenance disruptions even as non-mining sectors rebounded.

Equities

Since 1930, the S&P 500 has gained an average of 5.6% in the fourth quarter of midterm years, nearly double its 2.9% average across all years.

Rates

Retail investors made their largest-ever rotation into long-duration Treasury ETFs, led by record inflows into TLT.

Energy

Record diesel prices are squeezing farmers, truckers, and small businesses.

Global Developments

The US dollar remains the dominant reserve currency.
